name: Tender Infrastructure
description: A sprawling 6-hour documentary assembled over three years by journalist-filmmaker Celestine Adeyemi-Brandt, Tender Infrastructure maps the informal care networks of the Shelf — the unlicensed medical practitioners, the communal food synthesis co-ops, the mutual aid circuits that sustain Tier 1 life outside corporate provision. The film treats these structures not as poverty workarounds but as sophisticated social technologies that predate and outperform corporate welfare models. Its central argument — that the Shelf has already solved problems the Spire pretends don't exist — is what made it dangerous.
cultural_impact: Tender Infrastructure is the most complete existing record of Shelf social infrastructure from the 2190s and has been used by urban sociologists, activists, and community organizers as a foundational document — its 6-hour runtime is considered essential rather than excessive.
story_hooks: Celestine Adeyemi-Brandt was released from corporate detention in 2201 but has been living under a pseudonym; someone has found her and wants to use her film's maps to dismantle the networks she documented.

A Tier 4 urban planning firm has acquired an unauthorized copy of Tender Infrastructure and is reverse-engineering the Shelf's mutual aid models for a corporate product — the party must decide what to do with this information.

One of the film's subjects has been contacted by a Vantablack producer who wants to adapt their story into a licensed neural-feed drama — the subject wants advice on whether to engage, and what it would cost them.
